summary: Single-author industry paper (Zinnia) on the 'LLM Wiki' pattern: compile a document corpus into a persistent wiki and serve it from a KV cache to a local model. It uses Llama 3.1 8B Q5_K_M on one Apple M4 Pro. Full-context (FC) beats a fixed-chunk RAG baseline on 30 editorially compiled insurance articles (Policygenius) but loses on 80 raw documents per RepLiQA topic. Blind Claude Sonnet compilation into wikis loses far more quality than either baseline. WiCER (compile, probe one QA per document, diagnose score-1 failures, pin the dropped facts, recompile) is reported to recover 80% of the lost quality. Claude Sonnet is compiler, diagnoser and judge.

claims.claim: On a curated 30-article corpus, full-context KV-cache inference beats RAG (4.38 vs 4.08/5) with 7.3x faster TTFT
claims.evidence: §4: 240 QA pairs generated by Claude Sonnet and judged by Claude Sonnet; greedy decoding, one run; the RAG baseline uses fixed-size chunking without reranking (acknowledged).

claims.claim: At 80 raw documents, FC quality falls below RAG (3.47 vs 3.64; RAG wins 13 of 15 topics, 2 tied)
claims.evidence: §5 on RepLiQA, 400 QA per topic. The 'document-count crossover' framing is confounded: the two settings also differ in corpus type (editorially compiled vs raw), QA source (Sonnet-generated vs RepLiQA) and domain, so document count is not isolated.

claims.claim: Blind LLM compilation into a wiki catastrophically drops facts (2.14-2.32 vs 3.46 for FC raw; 53-60% score-1 answers), and the compiler over-compresses well beyond the requested ratio
claims.evidence: Table 3: 51 wikis over 17 topics, 6,800 QA per condition. Targets of 75/50/25% yielded 35.4/12.2/8.2% actual length. This is the best-supported result, but it conflates 'compilation' with 'compression to 8-35%': no condition compiles at the requested ratio, so the gap at faithful compression is unknown.

claims.claim: One to two WiCER iterations recover 80% of the quality lost by blind compilation (mean 3.24 vs 3.47 FC raw) and cut catastrophic failures by 55% relative
claims.evidence: Table 4 is 'mean quality on 80 probes each', the same probes whose score-1 failures drive diagnosis and pinning, with no held-out questions. The FC raw denominator (3.47) is measured on all 400 questions per topic, so the recovery ratio mixes an in-sample numerator with an out-of-sample baseline. Best iteration per topic is selected post hoc. The NeurIPS checklist states a different headline ('71% across eight topics').

claims.claim: Targeted diagnosis, not pinning per se, drives the gains (+0.95 vs +0.16 for random pinning)
claims.evidence: Table 5 is again in-sample on the 80 probes. The random control pins a random passage from a random source document, not from the failed probe's own document, so it is a weak control. Diagnosed pins are effectively the answers to the evaluation probes. Blind baselines shift between runs 'due to LLM compiler non-determinism', but this variance is not quantified.

patterns.note: LLM summarization of a document corpus into a compact wiki is measured against raw full context and RAG on the same 6,800 questions and loses by 1.1-1.3 points, with score-1 rates tripling (Table 3). This is corpus compaction rather than agent-trajectory compaction, and over-compression is confounded with compaction. It agrees with 2607.26072 that compressed summaries lose facts.

A persistent compiled domain-knowledge artifact is the paper's subject. Blind compilation is clearly worse than raw documents or RAG. The refined version narrows the gap only on in-sample probes, and at its best still trails RAG (3.18 vs 3.64 in the ablation set). Domain is insurance, news and RepLiQA topics, not software.

An untuned fixed-chunk RAG baseline loses to full context on 30 curated documents but beats full context (13/15 topics) and every compiled wiki on 80 raw documents. Corpus size is confounded with corpus type, and there is only one model.
Proposes the evaluate-diagnose-pin loop for a persistent wiki memory, including using production query streams as continuous probes. Its benefit is shown only in-sample.

Claude Sonnet judge vs one domain expert on 100 items: r=0.94, 75% exact agreement. Only 9 of those items are WiCER outputs, the condition carrying the headline. The judge model also compiled and diagnosed the wikis it scores, and generated the Policygenius QA.

methodology.sample: Policygenius: 30 articles, 240 QA. RepLiQA: 17 topics x 80 documents x 400 QA (6,800 per condition); WiCER on 80 probes per topic
methodology.baselines: Full-context raw, fixed-chunk RAG without reranking, blind compilation, random pinning
methodology.models: Llama 3.1 8B Q5_K_M (reader, local llama.cpp on Apple M4 Pro); Claude Sonnet (QA generator for Policygenius, compiler, diagnoser, judge)
methodology.variance: Greedy decoding, single run; cross-topic SD only. Compiler non-determinism acknowledged but not measured; no CIs or significance tests
methodology.ablations: Diagnosed vs random pinning (in-sample); compression level
methodology.contamination_controls: Compiler blind to evaluation questions for the blind wikis only; WiCER intentionally optimizes on the evaluation probes

standards.peer_review: Not peer reviewed; NeurIPS-format checklist included (and inconsistent with the abstract)
standards.artifacts: Code 'will be released'; no repository URL. Appendix C lists only the FC and RAG benchmark scripts, not the compiler or WiCER loop

biases.detail: WiCER and its ablation are scored on the same probes used to diagnose and pin facts, and the best iteration is chosen per topic, with no held-out split.
One 8B reader on one machine; one judge and compiler family.
Single runs; compiler non-determinism visibly moves blind baselines between Tables 4 and 5 but is not quantified.
Code promised but not linked; the reproducibility appendix omits WiCER itself.
Recovery ratio divides an 80-probe in-sample score by a 400-question baseline gap.
Judge validation includes only 9 WiCER items from one human rater, and the judge is the same model family that produced the artifacts.

coi.affiliations: Zinnia Tech Solutions (insurance software); single author
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: None of the author's; uses Llama 3.1, Claude Sonnet, llama.cpp
coi.detail: No affiliated product is evaluated; the insurance-domain choice reflects the employer but confers no evident advantage.

verdict_reason: Off-topic for this KB: knowledge compilation for document QA by a local model, not software development with LLMs or agents, nor its human side. Independently, the headline WiCER result (80% recovery, 55% fewer catastrophic failures, diagnosis vs random pinning) is measured in-sample on the diagnostic probes, with best-iteration selection, against baselines measured on a different question set, and with no released implementation.
applicability: A caution for the harness's knowledge-capture step, not evidence for it. If the team has an LLM condense domain material (healthcare-education content rules, ingestion contracts, onboarding notes) into domain cards or a wiki that agents load instead of the sources, expect silent fact loss and overshoot of any requested length. The robust result here is that blind compilation lost 1.1-1.3 points versus raw sources or plain retrieval. So: (1) keep source documents retrievable alongside any compiled card; (2) gate each generated card on a held-out question set written by a domain expert, not on the questions used to fix it; (3) check actual vs requested length. The probe-and-pin refinement loop is a plausible maintenance mechanism but is unproven out of sample.
